status_summary: Public Law 119-21, enacted 2025-07-04 through budget reconciliation, changed SNAP (Title I, Subtitle A) together with commodity and crop insurance programs (Subtitles C and E) in one act (govinfo). H.R. 7567, introduced 2026-02-13, keeps a nutrition title alongside the commodity title, with both running generally through 2031, so the two subjects were not separated (govinfo; CRS). The bill had a committee markup (ordered reported 34-17 on 2026-03-05) and a structured rule adopted 216-210 on 2026-04-29 that made 57 of 371 submitted amendments in order before House passage 224-200 on 2026-04-30 (CRS; House Rules Committee), and a 2026-04-27 Statement of Administration Policy supported swift passage without addressing process or separation (whitehouse.gov). After House passage, the Senate Agriculture Committee released updated text of the Agricultural Act of 2026 on 2026-07-31 and advanced it 12-11 on 2026-09-16 with nutrition programs including SNAP still in the bill, leaving Senate passage and reconciliation with the House bill outstanding (Senate committee release; The National News Desk).

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 was enacted by reconciliation; its Title I (Agriculture) includes SNAP changes (Subtitle A, Nutrition) together with commodity and crop insurance changes.
H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, was introduced with twelve titles including Title IV (Nutrition).
The House Agriculture Committee ordered H.R. 7567 reported, as amended, 34-17, after a markup that included the nutrition title.
The Office of Management and Budget issued a Statement of Administration Policy supporting swift passage of H.R. 7567.
The House adopted a structured rule (H. Res. 1224) for H.R. 7567, 216-210.
The House passed H.R. 7567, 224-200, with the nutrition title still in the bill.

Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman John Boozman releases updated text of the Agricultural Act of 2026 (Farm Bill 2.0) and announces a business meeting for 2026-08-06 to mark it up; the release describes a longer timeline for states to restore SNAP benefit integrity.

title: Insist on an open farm bill process and separate farm from nutrition reauthorization
uncertainties: Judged diverged because the enacted reconciliation route combined nutrition and commodity changes and the pending bill keeps one nutrition title on the same 2031 horizon, which runs opposite to the recommended separation, and the administration's statement supported the combined bill. The committee markup and a structured floor rule with amendments made in order are consistent with part of the open-process element, so whether the whole record is diverged or proposed is a judgment call. A news report indicates Senate Agriculture Committee deliberations in August 2026 ended without a bill; the exact date was not printed, so it is not a timeline event, and CRS (June 2026) reports no Senate markup in the 119th Congress. CRS does not discuss separation explicitly. The separation element also appears in c10-02 as part of the Mandate's description of an ideal USDA; this record carries the process and timeline elements on pages 297 and 298. Update 2026-10-29: the Senate committee vote was read through a The National News Desk report syndicated on okcfox.com, not through Senate or congress.gov records, which were not opened; the bill's title-by-title summary linked from the 2026-07-31 Senate committee release was not read, so how SNAP is organized in the Senate text was not confirmed from the bill itself. A California Ag Today report on aginfo.net (2026-09-10) and the sibling record's news source said the 2018 farm bill extension was set to expire 2026-09-30. An article on agrolatam.com (2026-10-02), a synthesis of other outlets' reporting and treated as an unverified lead, reports that the extension lapsed on 2026-09-30 without a replacement or new extension, that the Senate bill was reported and placed on the calendar on 2026-09-24, and that the chambers had not reconciled their bills; these points were not confirmed on a qualifying source in this review, and a lapse of authority is not itself a government action. No enacted farm bill or new extension was identified. Stage unchanged because the Senate bill also combines nutrition with farm programs.
